subject: series
synopsis: Paul Kupperberg's 1983 fantasy series set in pre-sinking Atlantis, following the powerful wizard Arion against forces threatening the ancient world. Solid but unremarkable Bronze Age sword-and-sorcery.
author: Paul Kupperberg

subject: series
synopsis: Yuto Tsukuda and Shun Saeki's cooking manga is one of the most exhilarating series in the medium — culinary competition executed with superhero-level dramatic intensity. The dish descriptions and cooking explanations are genuinely educational.
author: Yuto Tsukuda

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Whittington and Ernie Bushmiller's strip about the glamorous flapper Fritzi Ritz; notable as the strip from which Nancy (Fritzi's niece) spun off to dominate.
author: Larry Whittington

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey and Tom Scioli's Jack Kirby tribute series is one of Image's finest — cosmic superhero concepts executed with Kirby's raw energy and philosophical ambition, but filtered through modern sensibility.
author: Joe Casey

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's archive collection of pre-code horror comics. Essential for horror history — the source material is lurid, inventive, and often genuinely disturbing in ways later code-era comics couldn't be.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ron Marz's series about Kyle Rayner as the Ion entity rather than a Green Lantern. Interesting power exploration but limited narrative scope.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Fury's 1989-1993 series: Bob Harras's Deltite Affair, then D.G. Chichester's espionage stories against Hydra and AIM.
author: D. G. Chichester, Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the animated series. Paul Dini and Scott McCloud's contributions especially are excellent; the animated style forces clarity and economy that suits superhero stories.
author: Scott McCloud

subject: series
synopsis: Ray Palmer as DC's size-changing physicist. The silver-age Gardner Fox and Gil Kane run is charming puzzle-oriented sci-fi; the Gail Simone Ryan Choi revival is the modern standout.
author: Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: The official graphic novel adaptation of Robert Jordan's The Eye of the World — the first volume of the Wheel of Time fantasy epic — by Chuck Dixon and various artists, capturing the scope of Jordan's world-building.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's America's Best Comics series about a science hero — a loving homage to pulp sci-fi and the science hero tradition. Chris Sprouse's clear-line art is perfect; Moore's nostalgia is never saccharine.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and James Robinson's 2002 Hawkman revival with Rags Morales — Carter Hall and Hawkgirl's reincarnation saga in St. Roch — later Gray and Palmiotti.
author: Justin Gray, Jimmy Palmiotti

subject: series
synopsis: The 2007 Brave and the Bold team-up series: Mark Waid and George Pérez's opening arcs, then J. Michael Straczynski's character pairings.
author: Bob Haney, Bill Finger

subject: series
synopsis: Adventure Comics volume 3 (2009-2011): Geoff Johns's Superboy in Smallville, then Paul Levitz's Legion of Super-Heroes.
author: Paul Levitz, Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Avengers volume 3 (1998-2004): Kurt Busiek and George Pérez's Heroes Return revival — Morgan Le Fay, Ultron Unlimited, the Kang Dynasty — then Geoff Johns.
author: Brian Michael Bendis, Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Elektra's second ongoing (2001-2004): Bendis and Austen's MAX-style opening, then Greg Rucka's Introspect and Robert Rodi.
author: Greg Rucka, Robert Rodi

subject: series
synopsis: Archie's 1997-1999 Sabrina series tied to the live-action sitcom, with Salem the talking cat.
author: Frank Doyle, George Gladir

subject: series
synopsis: DC's second Star Trek series (1989-1996), continuing the original crew's movie-era voyages, largely written by Peter David and Howard Weinstein.
author: Peter David, Howard Weinstein

subject: series
synopsis: Mignola-verse ongoing: Abe Sapien wanders an America collapsing into Hell on Earth, searching for his origins amid frog-monster plagues.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: Archie's 2000s Sabrina series, later rebooted in manga style by Tania del Rio.
author: Frank Doyle, George Gladir

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's free web anthology hosted on MySpace (2007-2010), serializing short stories by Mignola, Joss Whedon and others.
author: Randy Stradley, Steve Mattsson

subject: series
synopsis: Marguerite Bennett's sequel to DC Bombshells. Expands the WWII-era female hero universe with more global scope.
author: Marguerite Bennett

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's collection of Tenth Doctor comics stories. Faithful to David Tennant's Doctor; competent licensed comics work.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's prestige fantasy and science fiction anthology magazine (1980–1986) that allowed creator ownership and published fully painted, adult-oriented stories; a peer to Heavy Metal in ambition if not longevity.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tini Howard's Krakoa-era take on Excalibur with Betsy Braddock as Captain Britain navigating the intersection of mutant politics and Arthurian magic.
author: Tini Howard

subject: series
synopsis: Kumo Kagyu's controversial dark fantasy follows an obsessive warrior who only kills goblins after his village was massacred by them, contrasted against lighter adventuring parties in the same world. Deliberately subverts cozy fantasy genre expectations with brutal violence.
author: Kumo Kagyu

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Mackie's series set in an alternate Marvel universe with divergent X-Men history. Interesting alternate takes on familiar characters; plotting is more ambitious than the execution.
author: Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's original 1992 Rai: the armored guardian of 41st-century Japan, spinning out of Magnus Robot Fighter and tying into Unity.
author: Matt Kindt

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroyuki Takei's complete shonen epic: Yoh Asakura and his samurai-ghost partner compete in the Shaman Fight to become Shaman King.

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen fantasy series about an archer seeking five fragments of a powerful weapon. Ron Marz's writing and Greg Land's art (before he became controversial) make for polished adventure.
author: Ron Marz, Ian Edginton

subject: series
synopsis: The relaunched Ultimate Universe Ultimates series following the new roster of heroes in a restructured Marvel universe after the events of Ultimate End, setting up the new Ultimate line.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: DC's supernatural anthology series from 1969–1978, hosted by three witches—Mordred, Mildred, and Cynthia—featuring horror tales in the EC Comics tradition.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's 2000 Captain Marvel: Genis-Vell, bonded to Rick Jones, gains cosmic awareness and descends into madness.
author: Arnold Drake, Mike Friedrich

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns's warm, legacy-focused revival. The JSA as mentors and living history — older heroes passing skills to next-generation characters — is an effective and emotionally resonant premise.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Silvestri's 1993 Image ongoing for the cybernetically enhanced rebels fighting the Cyberdata corporation.
author: Matt Hawkins, Bryan Hill

subject: series
synopsis: The third volume of Dark Horse's flagship anthology (2014-2016), serializing shorts and creator-owned features in each issue.
author: Randy Stradley, John Arcudi

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jolley's 2004 Firestorm: Detroit teen Jason Rusch inherits the nuclear matrix, later bonding with Martin Stein.
author: Stuart Moore, Dan Jolley

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander's 1990 Hawkworld ongoing: Thanagarian officer Katar Hol on Earth, a gritty sci-fi cop take on Hawkman.
author: John Ostrander, Timothy Truman

subject: series
synopsis: The Rebirth Flash (2016-2023): Joshua Williamson's long Barry Allen run with the Speed Force wars, then Jeremy Adams's return of Wally West at #750.

subject: series
synopsis: Judd Winick's 2008 reunion of the classic Teen Titans as adults against Trigon, later Eric Wallace's Deathstroke-led Titans.
author: Chris Claremont, Archie Goodwin

subject: series
synopsis: Hajime Isayama's manga about humanity's last survivors behind walls against giant humanoid monsters is one of the most gripping narratives in recent comics history. The revelations about the true nature of the world are brilliantly layered.
author: Hajime Isayama

subject: series
synopsis: Harold Sakuishi's music manga about a teenage boy joining a band. One of the finest music-themed manga — the live performance sequences crackle with energy and the character relationships are deeply felt.
author: Harold Sakuishi

subject: series
synopsis: Milestone's gang-turned-superheroes from the Dakota City big bang. Ivan Velez Jr.'s series deals with race, sexuality, and gang dynamics with a frankness unusual in mainstream superhero comics.
author: Ivan Velez Jr.

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's take on the Etrigan the Demon. Byrne's art is strong; the plotting leans heavily on DC mythology.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld's Image founding-era Bloodstrike spinoff featuring the assassin characters from the main series in standalone missions, a product of the maximalist early-1990s Image aesthetic.
author: Rob Liefeld

subject: series
synopsis: Will Pfeifer's 2005 mini-series sending DC's Captain Atom into the Wildstorm universe, where his presence threatens to destroy that world. An interesting cross-universe character study.
author: Will Pfeifer

subject: series
synopsis: The original 1988 Checkmate: the government's chess-ranked covert agency spun out of Vigilante, in Paul Kupperberg's spy actioner.
author: Paul Kupperberg, Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: John Stewart's recent solo series in the Lantern line. Phillip Kennedy Johnson builds on the character's military background and moral seriousness.
author: Phillip Kennedy Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's Marvel NOW! Guardians of the Galaxy (2013-2015): Star-Lord's team with Iron Man and Angela, through The Black Vortex.
author: Jim Valentino, Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the Justice League Unlimited animated series. Solid all-ages superhero stories.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and John Cassaday's Wildstorm masterpiece follows the 'archaeological team of the impossible' — three super-powered investigators uncovering the secret history of a world shaped by pulp fiction, science fiction, and superhero myth. A postmodern tour de force that is simultaneously a love letter to and deconstruction of the entire history of popular genre fiction.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Budiansky's Marvel series about an alien guardian who protects a human's mind while he sleeps. An underrated concept with solid Ditko-esque visual design.
author: Bob Budiansky

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's trade collection reprinting Marvel's classic Conan the Barbarian issues. Essential for fans who prefer collected format; Roy Thomas/Barry Windsor-Smith and John Buscema era material.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Collin Kelly and Jackson Lanzing's 2024 NYX: young mutants of the post-Krakoa diaspora, led by Laura Kinney and Kamala Khan, making lives in New York City.
author: Joe Quesada, Collin Kelly

subject: series
synopsis: Ghost Rider volume 2 (1990-1998): Danny Ketch becomes the Spirit of Vengeance in Howard Mackie and Mark Texeira's 90s hit.
author: Jenny Blake Isabella, Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's high-concept sci-fi series following Atlantean survivors who slept for millennia and awakened to find Earth transformed by alien civilizations wielding the sigil. Written by Mark Waid and Chuck Dixon with art by Steve Epting, it blended hard science-fiction concepts with CrossGen's signature mythological framework.
author: Chuck Dixon, Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Telltale's adventure game prequel adapted to comics. Matthew Sturges and Dave Justus's prequel exploring Bigby Wolf's early days as Fabletown's sheriff is a worthy companion to the main series.
author: Matthew Sturges, Dave Justus

subject: series
synopsis: A collected edition of the Green Arrow/Black Canary ongoing series by Judd Winick and Cliff Chiang, focusing on Oliver Queen and Dinah Lance's marriage and the adventures that test their partnership.
author: Judd Winick

subject: series
synopsis: The official comics-only continuation of the Friendship is Magic animated series, picking up after the show's finale with the original Mane 6 cast.
author: Katie Cook, Heather Nuhfer

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1940s-60s romance/humor comics starring the bright, peppy Patsy Walker. Historically interesting as an early Marvel teen humor comic; later became Hellcat.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hal Foster's gorgeous illustrated strip set in the age of King Arthur; celebrated for Foster's breathtaking painterly art and its epic multigenerational storytelling across centuries of Arthurian legend.
author: Hal Foster

subject: series
synopsis: One of DC's long-running Silver Age science fiction anthology series, featuring mostly standalone sci-fi tales and notable as the home of Adam Strange. Also the title of a celebrated 2020 Tom King/Mitch Gerads limited series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's colorized reprints of Eastman and Laird's original Mirage Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comics.

subject: series
synopsis: Taiki Kawakami's manga adaptation of Fuse's light novel. Isekai fantasy with unusually competent world-building; the protagonist's slime abilities create genuinely creative problem-solving.
author: Fuse

subject: series
synopsis: Jerry Ordway's excellent 1990s revamp of Captain Marvel, treating Billy Batson's transformation with genuine charm and the Fawcett mythology with respectful imagination. A warm-hearted superhero series that balanced modern storytelling with golden-age whimsy.
author: Jerry Ordway

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Spider-Man series featuring both Peter Parker and Miles Morales teaming up as the Spectacular Spider-Men, exploring what happens when two Spider-Men share one city and one legacy.
author: Greg Weisman, Nick Lowe

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's black-and-white magazine companion to Master of Kung Fu. Shang-Chi plus Iron Fist and other martial arts heroes in longer-form stories. Some excellent material from Doug Moench and Paul Gulacy.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Russell and Bob Quinn's satirical 2024 X-Factor, a government-backed, publicity-driven mutant team in the From the Ashes era.
author: Bob Layton, Louise Jones Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: Full-color comic stories of Jolly Blackburn's Knights of the Dinner Table, the hapless tabletop gaming group.

subject: series
synopsis: Gamon Sakurai's manga about immortal demi-humans hunted by the Japanese government. Tense sci-fi thriller with inventive action and genuinely compelling moral ambiguity about the protagonist.
author: Gamon Sakurai

subject: series
synopsis: The classic Archie split-focus series on Riverdale's two leading ladies. Mid-century American teen humor with a romance comics twist.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: WildStorm's solo series following Marc Slayton, a veteran Kherubim warrior and former Team 7 operative, navigating the shadowy world of covert super-powered conflict after leaving government service. Part of the dense, interconnected WildStorm universe alongside Stormwatch and WildC.A.T.s, with high-octane action typical of the mid-90s Image era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Cassidy trapped in a demon suit. Gary Cohn and Dan Mishkin's original run is charming 80s DC humor-superhero fare; later uses of the character lean darker.
author: Gary Cohn, Dan Mishkin

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer's controversial run that revealed Steve Rogers as a Hydra sleeper agent. Ambitious but divisive; the resolution was unsatisfying to many readers.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Taku Kuwabara's manga about airship crews hunting dragons for food. Cozy adventure with meticulous food and hunting culture world-building; dragon cooking descriptions are genuinely appetizing.
author: Taku Kuwabara

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Amend's strip about the suburban Fox family, beloved for its sharp math/science/pop-culture humor and the nerdy teenage son Jason's obsession with computers, video games, and Star Wars.
author: Bill Amend

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's self-published digital continuation of his celebrated X-Men run, exploring alternate timeline stories with the characters he helped define in the late 1970s. A passion project from a major comics figure revisiting the material that made him famous.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' literary comics anthology — one of the finest American comics magazines of the 2000s. Published work by Anders Nilsen, Dash Shaw, and many other significant literary cartoonists.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's Krakoa-era series following Kate Pryde captaining the Marauders as they run a mutant underground railroad, featuring the prolonged mystery of Kate's death and resurrection and strong political subtext.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: ONE's webcomic (drawn by Yusuke Murata for the manga) is a brilliant parody of shonen power fantasies — Saitama can defeat anyone in one punch, and that makes heroism meaningless. Rich philosophical subtext under the comedy.
author: ONE

subject: series
synopsis: Takehiko Inoue's basketball manga is one of the finest sports manga ever created. Hanamichi Sakuragi's arc from delinquent to vital team player is executed with extraordinary craft.
author: Takehiko Inoue

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule and Tony Daniel's series exploring the romantic and heroic partnership between Superman and Wonder Woman, combining Daniel's polished superhero action with Soule's knack for character dynamics. A confident title that takes the power-couple premise seriously and generates genuine tension from their fundamentally different worldviews.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Hiromu Arakawa's manga adaptation of Yoshiki Tanaka's Persian-inspired fantasy epic. Arakawa brings her Full Metal Alchemist craft to a sweeping historical military narrative.
author: Yoshiki Tanaka, Hiromu Arakawa

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Van Hamme and Grzegorz Rosinski's Belgian epic fantasy about a Nordic hero of alien origin. One of Europe's finest fantasy comics — beautiful realistic art and rich mythological storytelling.
author: Jean Van Hamme

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Mike Allred's satirical superhero series about celebrity mutants is one of Marvel's most darkly funny and formally inventive titles. The Allred art is perfect for its campy menace.
author: Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas's late 80s DC series adding diverse WWII-era heroes to the All-Star Squadron. More culturally ambitious than most of the era; the Iron Munro/Fury relationship is genuinely interesting.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Chester Brown's Drawn and Quarterly series collects his early work including Ed the Happy Clown (darkly surreal) and gospel adaptations. A key work in literary Canadian comics.
author: Chester Brown

subject: series
synopsis: The spider-bite scientific vampire gets various solo series. Most are atmospheric horror-adjacent superhero work; the Tom Defalo and later David Hine runs are the better material.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel horror anthology that evolved into Man-Thing's primary showcase; early issues featured standalone supernatural stories before Steve Gerber's landmark run transformed it into a psychedelic swamp horror series exploring trauma and empathy.
author: Steve Gerber

subject: series
synopsis: Harvey Pekar's self-published autobiographical comic (1976-1991) of everyday Cleveland life as a file clerk, drawn by Crumb, Budgett, Dumm and others.
author: Harvey Pekar, Joyce Brabner

subject: series
synopsis: Anthony Oliveira's digital Infinity Comic about young heroes training at the Avengers Academy.
author: Anthony Oliveira

subject: series
synopsis: Yana Toboso's manga about a Victorian-era earl and his demonic butler. Gothic mystery with dark humor and impeccably researched period detail. Long-running and consistently entertaining.
author: Yana Toboso

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's 1996 series about Ivana Baiul's amoral Gen-Active teens, launched by Warren Ellis's first eight issues.
author: Michael Heisler, Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Ryohgo Narita's (Baccano!, Durarara!!) manga about a powerful necromancer who is reincarnated in the body of a Japanese criminal — forcing him to navigate Tokyo's underworld with magic in a modern world. Clever genre blending with Narita's signature ensemble plotting.
author: Ryohgo Narita

subject: series
synopsis: Satoru Noda's manga about a gold hunt in early 20th century Hokkaido is an extraordinary work — meticulous Ainu cultural research, kinetic action, dark humor, and food culture all woven together brilliantly.
author: Satoru Noda

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in comics series to the Ultimate Spider-Man animated series, offering all-ages adventures featuring the show's young Peter Parker and S.H.I.E.L.D. training.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Bedard's 2009 R.E.B.E.L.S.: Vril Dox leads a ragtag alien resistance against Starro the Conqueror, then Brainiac's legacy.
author: Tony Bedard, Brian Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Tania Del Rio's manga-influenced Sabrina the Teenage Witch series following the young witch's magic school adventures and romantic entanglements.
author: Tania Del Rio

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman and Nick Spencer's (later Andy Diggle's) crime series following Redmond — the world's greatest thief — who wants to quit the life, but finds that neither the criminal underworld nor the FBI will let him walk away.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's continuation of the classic Thundercats animated property, depicting the Lion-O and his companions facing new threats beyond Thundera.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Ken Wakui's manga about a man who can time-travel to his middle school years to save his girlfriend from a delinquent gang. Time-loop mechanics and gang dynamics combine effectively.
author: Ken Wakui

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Levitz's New 52 series following Power Girl and Huntress, revealed to be Karen Starr and Helena Wayne from Earth-2, stranded in the main DCU and trying to find their way home.
author: Paul Levitz

subject: series
synopsis: Leah Williams's sharp, personality-driven X-Factor series set on Krakoa, following the team investigating mutant deaths under the resurrection protocols. Williams wrote the ensemble with genuine wit and care for often-underused characters, making this one of the better Krakoa-era books.
author: Leah Williams

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroaki Samura's samurai epic: the cursed immortal swordsman Manji must kill a thousand evil men, bodyguarding the vengeful girl Rin across Edo Japan.

subject: series
synopsis: Prequel to Goblin Slayer chronicling the hero's first year of hunting goblins as a novice adventurer.

subject: series
synopsis: The Spectre, Jim Corrigan as the Wrath of God; our files credit John Ostrander and Tom Mandrake's dark 1990s run.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 'what if his X-Men run had continued uninterrupted?' alternate timeline. Nostalgic for longtime fans but inaccessible to newer readers; the divergence choices are often surprising.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Powers volume 2 at Marvel Icon (2004-2008): Bendis and Oeming's homicide detectives Walker and Pilgrim keep investigating superhuman crimes.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Batgirl (2011-2016): Gail Simone restores Barbara Gordon's mobility, then Stewart, Fletcher and Tarr's Batgirl of Burnside.
author: Scott Peterson, Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: Duane Swierczynski's 2008 Cable: Nathan Summers flees through the future raising the infant mutant messiah Hope, pursued by Bishop.
author: Jeph Loeb, Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Gerard Jones's 1991 Wonder Man: Avenger Simon Williams balances Hollywood acting and super-heroics.
author: Gerard Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Wood and Olivier Coipel's 2013 X-Men: Storm, Rogue, Kitty, Psylocke, Rachel and Jubilee face Arkea, then G. Willow Wilson's run.
author: Brian Wood, G. Willow Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone's Marvel series follows Alex Hayden, the amnesiac mercenary Agent X, whose healing factor links him to Deadpool as he takes over the bodyguard-for-hire outfit Agency X. A wisecracking action-comedy of assassins, double-crosses, and absurd violence.
author: Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Van Lente's 2012 Valiant relaunch: sheltered teen assassin Obadiah Archer teams with the hard-drinking immortal Armstrong against secret societies.

subject: series
synopsis: Dave Louapre and Dan Sweetman's Piranha Press anthology from DC's edgier imprint, weaving dark humor with surreal horror and social commentary in standalone tales about society's misfits. An interesting artifact of DC's brief experiment with underground-influenced alternative comics.
author: Dave Louapre

subject: series
synopsis: Eve Ewing's 2024 X-Men series set in the post-Krakoa era, centering on Kate Pryde reluctantly mentoring a small group of young mutants who missed the Krakoa years entirely. Praised for its character-driven approach, emotional intelligence, and Ewing's skill at building ensemble dynamics — a quieter, more intimate counterpoint to the era's bigger X-Men books.
author: Eve Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: The graphic novel adaptations of Elisabetta Dami's popular Italian children's book series about the mouse journalist Geronimo Stilton; colorful, adventure-filled children's comics.
author: Elisabetta Dami

subject: series
synopsis: The Harbinger-level powered team working for Project HARD Corps in the early Valiant Universe — mercenaries implanted with technology that channels psionic powers, battling Toyo Harada's Harbinger Foundation.
author: David Michelinie

subject: series
synopsis: Golden age Marvel Comics' original Human Torch (not Johnny Storm) — an android whose early adventures defined the pulpy style of Timely Comics. Historically essential.
author: Carl Burgos

subject: series
synopsis: Bruce Jones and Brent Anderson's acclaimed Ka-Zar series, widely considered the definitive take — a mature, humanistic adventure that used the jungle-lord premise for sophisticated character work and genuine emotional stakes rather than simple action.
author: Bruce Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Tomohito Oda's manga about a girl with severe social anxiety who wants to make 100 friends. Warm, funny, and genuinely insightful about social anxiety and the effort of connection.
author: Tomohito Oda

subject: series
synopsis: Ian Flynn's Archie Comics adaptation of the classic Capcom game. Better than its premise — Flynn knows the source material deeply and builds genuine character from thin game-story bones.
author: Ian Flynn

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel/Atlas Comics' long-running teen romance anthology following Patsy Walker and her glamorous rival Hedy Wolfe through the social dramas of high school and young adult life, in a style strongly influenced by Archie Comics. A defining title of Marvel's pre-superhero output; the series gained retroactive significance when Patsy Walker later became the Avenger Hellcat.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1977-1979 Tarzan: Roy Thomas and John Buscema adapting and extending Edgar Rice Burroughs's jungle lord.
author: Roy Thomas, David Anthony Kraft

subject: series
synopsis: The graphic novel spin-off of Geronimo Stilton focusing on Thea Stilton and the Thea Sisters, a group of female mouse students; adventure stories with a girl-power focus.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen and Caanan White's Avatar series imagines a World War II where Nazi Germany deploys 'ubers' — superhuman living weapons — in 1945, brutally altering the war's course. A grim, gory alternate history about superpowers as instruments of total war.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the Lynda Carter TV series. Marc Andreyko captures the show's empowerment message and period charm effectively.
author: Marc Andreyko

subject: series
synopsis: Set in a dystopian future, this series followed a new team of X-Men in 2099 written by John Francis Moore, part of Marvel's ambitious 2099 imprint exploring corporate dystopia and cyberpunk themes.
author: John Francis Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spurrier's acclaimed run on X-Men Legacy, reinventing the series as a solo book starring Legion (David Haller), Professor X's extraordinarily powerful but fractured son, as a psychedelic character study about identity, mental illness, and the nature of heroism.
author: Simon Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: Karl and Barbara Kesel's 1989 Hawk and Dove: Hank Hall and the new Dove, Dawn Granger, as avatars of chaos and order.
author: Barbara Randall Kesel, Karl Kesel

subject: series
synopsis: Reginald Hudlin's 2005 Black Panther: T'Challa defends Wakanda from Klaw's invasion, marries Storm, and passes the mantle to Shuri.
author: Reginald Hudlin, Cory Sedlmeier

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1990-1993 quarterly anthology of fill-in and inventory stories starring assorted heroes.
author: Scott Lobdell, Sue Flaxman

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott and Mark Bagley's 2022 Spider-Man, tied to End of the Spider-Verse and the return of Spider-Boy.

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Foxe's 2024 Spider-Woman: after Gang War, Hydra targets Jessica Drew's family and she returns to San Francisco.
author: Marv Wolfman, Mark Gruenwald

subject: series
synopsis: The original Teen Titans (1966-1978): Robin, Kid Flash, Wonder Girl, Aqualad and Speedy in Silver Age teen adventures.
author: Geoff Johns, Sean McKeever

subject: series
synopsis: Wonder Woman's Rebirth series (2016-2023): Greg Rucka's Year One and The Lies, then Robinson, G. Willow Wilson and Mariko Tamaki, reaching #750.
author: William Marston, Alice Marble

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1992 Shadowman: New Orleans jazz musician Jack Boniface becomes a voodoo-powered guardian of the night.
author: Cullen Bunn, Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: The Fantastic Four annuals: Lee and Kirby's Sub-Mariner epic and Reed and Sue's wedding, then later extras.
author: Mark Gruenwald, Steve Englehart

subject: series
synopsis: Zom 100: a burned-out office worker greets the zombie apocalypse as liberation and sets out to complete a bucket list before he dies.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel/Atlas pre-code horror anthology running 1950–1954, featuring short supernatural tales that rode the horror comics wave popularized by EC Comics. An important historical document of the Atlas era showcasing early work by artists who would later define Marvel's silver age, produced before the Comics Code Authority ended the genre.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Steven Seagle's 1997 Alpha Flight relaunch: a new government-run roster under Department H, mysteries and all.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's deluxe hardcover reprints of Warren Publishing's legendary Creepy horror anthology magazine, originally published 1964–1983 under the editorial vision of Archie Goodwin. Features classic horror tales by Neal Adams, Reed Crandall, Berni Wrightson, and other giants of the art form. An essential archive for fans of horror comics history.
author: Various

subject: series

synopsis: Hank Ketcham's beloved American newspaper comic strip, first published in 1951, following the incorrigible five-year-old Dennis Mitchell and his long-suffering neighbor Mr. Wilson. One of the most widely recognized and syndicated strips in comics history, built on gentle, timeless humor about childhood mischief; continued after Ketcham's 2001 death by his studio.
author: Hank Ketcham

author: Warren Ellis

synopsis: Gerard Jones's unusual 1992 GL series following John Stewart as the protector of a mosaic world on Oa where alien communities have been transplanted, notable for its experimental structure and psychological depth.

synopsis: Tim Seeley's horror-action series following Cassie Hack — a survivor of slasher violence who hunts supernatural killers called slashers — and her gentle giant partner Vlad. A loving deconstruction of slasher film conventions that builds genuine emotional depth and character complexity beneath its genre-horror surface, earning a devoted cult following across multiple publishers.
author: Tim Seeley
